en: An object with a mass of 60 kilograms on Earth experiences a gravitational pull of 588 newtons, but only 98 newtons on the Moon.
Traveling at 300,000 kilometers per second, light from the Sun takes exactly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to cross the 150 million kilometers to Earth.
Sound travels through water at 1,480 meters per second, which is more than four times faster than its speed of 343 meters per second in air.
A block and tackle pulley system with four supporting rope segments multiplies your input force by four, letting you lift a 400-newton box with just 100 newtons.
Sliding a heavy box across rough concrete requires about 40 newtons of force, but sliding it across smooth ice requires only 5 newtons due to lower friction.
The electrical signal in a copper wire travels at about 270,000 kilometers per second, which is roughly 90 percent the speed of light in a vacuum.
Heating one kilogram of water by one degree Celsius requires about five times more heat energy than heating one kilogram of dry sand by the same amount.
A 1,000-kilogram car moving at 10 meters per second has 50,000 joules of kinetic energy, exactly twice as much as a 500-kilogram horse running at the same speed.
Pushing a cart up a 10-meter long ramp that is 2 meters high requires only one-fifth of the lifting force needed to raise it straight up.
A strong neodymium magnet produces a magnetic field of 1 Tesla, which is 20,000 times stronger than Earth's natural magnetic field of 50 microteslas.
Because Jupiter's gravity is 2.5 times stronger than Earth's, a student whose weight is 400 newtons on Earth would weigh 1,000 newtons on Jupiter.
A normal conversation produces sound at 60 decibels, while a jet engine produces 140 decibels, making the jet engine's sound one hundred million times more intense.
